semantics.identity_rule: This member gives an exact owner-scoped identity to the literal Flow token without adding semantics beyond the owning Flow reference field and the preserved source literal.
semantics.interpretation_rule: Consumers may use this identity as an opaque declared Flow symbol. No meaning may be inferred from spelling, whitespace, filename, path or similarity to another symbol.
semantics.authority_rule: A Flow symbol is descriptive/causal model data only and never grants runtime authority, capability, ownership or execution permission.
semantics.scope_rule: Identity is scoped semantically to the defining contract; identical source literals in another contract or another Flow-ref role are not automatically the same semantic identity.

topics.name: Causality
topics.purpose: Group explicit behavior-flow semantics that describe what causes what, under which conditions, and what happens next.

metadata.note: This defines how canonical causality is represented. It does not itself grant runtime execution authority.
metadata.dynamic_reference_rule: Concrete flow instances use the current step's explicit subflow_refs and resume_ref. This interpreter/meta-flow does not substitute placeholder strings into reference fields.

causal_fields.cause_ref: Explicit causal predecessor or causal source.
causal_fields.condition_ref: Explicit condition controlling whether a step/branch applies.
causal_fields.resume_ref: Explicit continuation point after subflow completion.

non_causal_sources: array position unless the owning field explicitly declares order semantic
semantics.mechanism_rule: A mechanism may compose existing Topics and reuse their semantics, but any new end-to-end causality introduced by that mechanism must be represented explicitly as flow data.
semantics.partial_flow_rule: A specification may reference an existing flow rather than duplicate it. It adds only the causal steps or branches that are genuinely new.

invariants.rule: Machine-significant execution causality is explicit structured flow data.
A flow describes causality but does not itself grant authority to execute effects.
Existing canonical flows are referenced rather than restated when no new causality is introduced.

hard_gates.condition: Execution order must be inferred from array position, prose, path, Topic or structural graph.
Multiple continuations are possible but no explicit condition or selection semantics distinguish them.
A nested mechanism must be inferred instead of being explicitly referenced as a subflow.
Continuation after a subflow requires guessing a resume point.
The existence of a flow is treated as authorization or runtime authority.

references.purpose: Separates structural graphs from execution causality.
Mechanism Topics may compose semantics but cannot imply causal order.

prose.summary: Makes behavior.flows the explicit canonical source for execution order, branches, subflows and continuation, allowing mechanism specifications to reuse existing Topics without duplicating their semantics.
notes: Unlocked until repository flows are migrated and checked for implicit causality.
Pass 8 formalized previously free Flow actor/data/target/condition/payload/result/error tokens as exact owner-scoped member identities while preserving every source literal.
